violations.text: Raw animal foods (such as shell eggs) were observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (such as cheeses and produce) in the walk-in refrigerator. Raw animal foods must be separated from raw ready-to-eat food such as vegetables during storage. Food items were rearranged during the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/13/2026

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils (ice machine) were observed with an accumulation of food and debris. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. The ice machine was taken out of service and emptied during the time of inspection. Establishment is to clean, sanitize, and allow unit to air dry prior to returning unit to service. New Violation. Correct By: 08/13/2026

Potato Salad, which was prepared in advance, was not cooled to 70 degrees Fahrenheit in 2 hours and then to 41 degrees Fahrenheit within 4 hours. Per PIC, potato salad was made the previous day and was observed held at 50 degrees Fahrenheit. Food item was voluntarily disposed of during the time of inspection. Proper cooling methods provided during the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/13/2026

The 1-door low boy was observed held at am ambient temperature of 60 degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Food items within the unit were evaluated and disposed of during the time of inspection. Establishment is not to store TCS food items in the unit until unit is able to maintain an ambient temperature of 41 degrees Fahrenheit or less. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/13/2026

Establishment was observed with marinated tuna steaks in the walk-in cooler that were placed in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP). Establishment does not have an approved HACCP plan for reduced oxygen packaging (ROP) of seafood items. Establishment is to cease practice of placing food items into ROP packing. Establishment is to work with food safety consultant to submit and receive approval for proposed HACCP plan for ROP packaging of seafood items. Food items were voluntarily disposed of during the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/13/2026

An employee was observed touching ready to eat food (sliced tomatoes) with bare hands. Food employees must not touch exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, single use gloves, or dispensing equipment. Food items were voluntarily disposed of during the time of inspection. Employee placed gloves on to complete the rest of their task. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/22/2025

Molluscan shellfish tags must be maintained for 90 days in chronological order and the date when the last shellfish was used from the bag must be noted on the shellfish tag. New Violation. Correct By: 07/22/2025
